div.head: §. 43. Of ſufferingsuffering ſeruantsservants to prouideprovide for themſeluesthemselves.
div.p: A fourth thing required of maſtersmasters in regard of their ſeruantsservants eſtateestate is, that after ſufficientsufficient ſeruiceservice done they ſuffersuffer their ſeruantsservants to prouideprovide for themſeluesthemselves. This IaakobJacob required of Laban as a moſtmost equallequal and reaſonablereasonable matter, ſayingsaying, Gen. 30. 30. when ſhallshall I prouideprovide for mine owneown houſehouse alſoalso? (as was §. 34. before noted in the generallgeneral.) This hath reſpectrespect eſpeciallyespecially vntounto ſuchsuch ſeruantsservants as hauehave beenebeen a long time with maſtersmasters as apprentiſesapprenticesapprentises, and ſpentspent their time, labour, and painespains only and wholly for their maſtersmasters good. Exod. 21. 2. Deut. 15. 12. Gods law tooketook expreſſeexpress order for ſuchsuch, that after certainecertain yeeresyears ſeruiceservice they ſhouldshould goego free. So doedo alſoalso the laweslaws of our land, eſpeciallyespecially the orders of London.

Herein lyethlieth a mainemain difference betwixt ſeruantsservants (who are vnderunder ſubiectionsubjection, and held to workework for their owneown good) and beaſtsbeasts (which are only for mans ſeruiceservice, and good.)

They therefore who are of a contrary mindemind, keeping ſeruantsservants Contrary. as long as poſſiblypossibly they can, eueneven all their life long vntounto hard labour, and vnderunder ſeruitudeservitude, deſeruedeserve to be ſeruedserved with beaſtsbeasts rather then men and women. This kindekind of maſtersmasters rigour to their ſeruantsservants is in particular noted to be IerJer. 34. 16, 17. one of the cauſescauses of that great indignation of God againſtagainst the IewesJews, whereby he was prouokedprovoked to giuegive them ouerover, as captiuescaptives to their enemies.

div.head: §. 44. Of kindneſſekindness to be ſhewedshowed to good ſeruantsservants.
div.p:
As maſtersmasters muſtmust giuegive that which is iuſtjust to all ſeruantsservants, ſoso that which is §. 20. equallequal to them that deſeruedeserve it: that is, they muſtmust be of an anſwerableanswerable mindemind and diſpoſitiondisposition to good, honeſthonest,
louingloving, kindekind, faithfullfaithful ſeruantsservants, who ſtandstand not ſoso much vponupon that which is exacted, as vponupon that which they are able to doedo for their maſtersmasters, and in that reſpectrespect, as they ſeesee occaſionoccasion doedo oft times much more then is exacted, or expected. GoodneſſeGoodness requireth goodneſſegoodness; good will, good will; and this is to doedo the ſamesame things. This kindekind of EquitieEquity conſiſtethconsisteth in theſethese and ſuchsuch like particulars.

1. MaſtersMasters muſtmust well eſteemeesteem of ſuchsuch good ſeruantsservants: and hauehave them in high account. Gen. 15. 2, 3. Abram accounted his old good faithfullfaithful ſeruantservant as his childechild, and till he had a childechild thought of making him his heireheir. Great was that eſteemeesteem which Potiphar
Qui vere patresfamilias ſuntsunt, ſeruisseruis in familia ſuasua tanquam filijs conſuluntconsulunt. Aug. de Ciu. Dei, l. 19. c. 16. had of IoſephJoseph, when of a bondſlauebondslave he made him ouerſeeroverseer ouerover his houſehouse, Gen. 39. 4. Why is the title Fatherfather giuengiven to maſtersmasters, (2. King. 5. 13.) and the title Sonnessons to ſeruantsservants, (IoſJos. 7. 19. & 1 Sam. 24. 16.) but to ſhewshow that ſeruantsservants ſhouldshould bearebear a child-like affection to their maſtersmasters, and that maſtersmasters ſhouldshould bearebear a fatherlike affection to ſuchsuch ſeruantsservants?

2. MaſtersMasters muſtmust take notice of the goodneſſegoodness, and kindneſſekindness of ſuchsuch ſeruantsservants: and manifeſtmanifest as much, both by giuinggiving them due praiſepraise, and a good reward: both which are noted in the patternepattern of that great maſtermaster who ſaidsaid, well done thou good
Matth. 25. 21. and faithfullfaithful ſeruantservant, thou haſthast beenebeen faithfullfaithful ouerover a few things, I will make thee ruler ouerover many things. Thus will thoſethose good ſeruantsservants be the more encouraged to hold on, and others will be mouedmoved to imitate them. This incouragementencouragement doth the ApoſtleApostle giuegive to all vnderunder authoritieauthority, doedo that which is good, and
Rom. 13. 3. thou ſhaltshalt hauehave praiſepraise of the ſamesame. Which phraſephrase implieth that gouernoursgovernors ought to praiſepraise thoſethose that doedo well.

3. If ſuchsuch ſeruantsservants be accuſedaccused of any hainousheinous crime, maſtersmasters muſtmust not raſhlyrashly giuegive credit thereto, but rather thorowlythoroughly ſiftsift, and examine the matter. Herein Potiphar exceedingly Gen. 39. 19. failed, and by that meanesmeans loſtlost ſuchsuch a ſeruantservant as he could neuernever get againeagain. If a good ſeruantservant doedo by occaſionoccasion ſlipslip, and commit a fault, his maſtermaster ought in wiſdomewisdom either to take no notice of it: or with ſomesome mildemild admonition paſſepass it ouerover: and not dealedeal with him as with a lewd, graceleſſegraceless ſeruantservant.

4. When ſuchsuch ſeruantsservants (their couenantedcovenanted time being expired) depart, their maſtersmasters muſtmust not let them goego away empty:
Deut. 15. 13.
but helpehelp them in their mariagemarriage (as MoſesMoses his maſtermaster did) or Exod. 2. 21. in their ſettingsetting vpup, as the great maſtermaster, who made his wiſewise and faithfullfaithful ſeruantservant ruler ouerover all his goods.
Matth. 24. 47.

div.head: §. 45. Of vnkindeunkind dealing with good ſeruantsservants.
div.p: VnworthyUnworthy they are of good and kindekind ſeruantsservants who are of a contrary mindemind: as many maſtersmasters areare. For

1. Some make no difference betwixt ſeruantsservants: but eſteemeesteem of bad and good all alike: they thinkethink that the beſtbest ſeruantsservants doedo but their duty, therefore no extraordinary reſpectrespect is to be borne towards them. But it is a point of wiſdomewisdom ſometimessometimes to account a duty as a kindneſſekindness: eſpeciallyespecially when good will of heart is ioynedjoined with outward performance of duty.

2. Others thinkethink it policy to take no notice of any ſeruantsservants extraordinary faithfulneſſefaithfulness and diligence to praiſepraise and reward the ſamesame, leſtlest it puffepuff them vpup too much. But there is much more fearefear of ſeruantsservants fainting, and waxing weary of doing good if they hauehave no incouragementencouragement, then of growing inſolentinsolent by incouragementencouragement.

3. Others will be more ready to checkecheck and rebuke ſuchsuch for eueryevery ſlipslip, and for failing in any thing, then others: becauſebecause others leſſeless regard their rebuke: whereby they ſhewshow want of wiſdomewisdom in well managing their authority.

4. Others when their ſeruantsservants are about to goego away, or to marry, or to ſetset vpup, will ſeekeseek ſomesome occaſionoccasion or other to fall out with them, of purpoſepurpose to ſendsend them away empty. Many will carry a fairefair face toward profitable ſeruantsservants till the time of recompencerecompense commethcometh, and then beginnebegin to frownefrown, as Laban
Gen. 31. 2. did. Yea ſoso farrefar are ſomesome maſtersmasters from ſeekingseeking the proſperityprosperity of faithfullfaithful, wiſewise, diligent, skilfullskilful ſeruantsservants, as they will hinder Sic cum inferiore viuas, quemadmodum tecum ſuperioremsuperiorem velles viuere. Senec. epiſtepist. 47. them in what they can, and keepekeep them downedown: fearing leſtlest as their ſeruantsservants riſerise, they themſeluesthemselves ſhouldshould decay and fall. TheſeThese are both vnkindeunkind, and vngratefullungrateful maſtersmasters. Would maſtersmasters be ſoso dealt with by their ſuperiourssuperiors? Thou oughteſtoughtest ſoso to liuelive with thy inferiourinferior, as thou wouldeſtwouldest hauehave thy ſuperioursuperior liuelive with thee.

p.hi: Hitherto of maſtersmasters duties. The reaſonsreasons to mouemove them to performeperform their duties follow.

div.head: §. 46. Of the ſubiectionsubjection vnderunder which maſtersmasters are.

p.hi: Knowing that your maſtermaster alſoalso is in heauenheaven: neither is there reſpectrespect of perſonspersons with him.

div.p: There is in generallgeneral but one reaſonreason alledgedalleged by the ApoſtleApostle, to prouokeprovoke maſtersmasters to doedo their duties, but it is ſoso laid downedown as it compriſethcompriseth other forcible reaſonsreasons vnderunder it.
The principallprincipal reaſonreason is taken from the ſubiectionsubjection wherein maſtersmasters are.
The other reaſonsreasons are taken from the deſcriptiondescription of that authority vnderunder which maſtersmasters are: for it is ſuchsuch an authority, as,
1. In relation to it there is no difference betwixt maſtermaster and ſeruantservant.
2. It is farrefar ſurpaſſingsurpassing all dignities on earth.
3. It is mouedmoved with no outward reſpectrespect of any thing.

The firſtfirst reaſonreason which declareth the ſubiectionsubjection of maſtersmasters, in that they hauehave a maſtermaster ouerover them, putteth them in mindemind of that account which they are to make, and reckoning which they are to giuegive of the well vſingusing of their authority, and of their cariagecarriage towards ſuchsuch as are vnderunder them. For they are but as ſtewardsstewards ouerover fellow ſeruantsservants: eueryevery one of them therefore ſhallshall hearehear this charge, giuegive an account of thy ſtewardſhipstewardship.
Luke 16. 2.
In this reſpectrespect this reaſonreason is both as a ſpurspur, and as a curbecurb vntounto maſtersmasters.

As a ſpurspur, to prickeprick them on forward conſcionablyconscionably to performeperform all thoſethose duties which are required of them: for they hauehave a maſtermaster that will take notice thereof, and reward them for it. As they approueapprove, and recompencerecompense the good ſeruiceservice which their ſeruantsservants doedo: ſoso much more will their maſtermaster approueapprove and recompencerecompense them if they doedo well. DoeDo maſtersmasters therefore lookelook that their ſeruantsservants ſhouldshould performeperform their duty? letLet them then performeperform theirs: for there is the ſamesame reaſonreason of both. Let this be applied to all the particular duties before mentioned.

It is alſoalso as a curbecurb, to reſtrainerestrain maſtersmasters from doing any thing
to their ſeruantsservants but what they can be able to iuſtifiejustify vntounto their owneown maſtermaster. With this curbecurb did God hold in the IſraelitesIsraelites, ſayingsaying, Leu. 25. 43. Thou ſhaltshalt not rule ouerover thy ſeruantservant with rigor, but ſhaltshalt fearefear thy God. IoſephJoseph was held in with it, when he ſaidsaid, Gen. 42. 18. This doedo and liuelive, for I fearefear God. And Nehemiah, when he ſaidsaid, Neh. 5. 15. The former GouernoursGovernors were chargeable to the people, but ſoso did not I becauſebecause of the fearefear of God. And IobJob, when he ſaidsaid, IobJob 31. 13, 14. If I did deſpiſedespise the cauſecause of my ſeruantservant, when God viſitethvisiteth, what ſhallshall I anſweranswer him? ThinkeThink of this ô maſtersmasters, when you are about to exact any thing of your ſeruantsservants that is not lawfulllawful or meet, when you are incenſedincensed and in paſſionpassion ſtirredstirred vpup to ſtrikestrike your ſeruantsservants vniuſtlyunjustly or cruelly, when you detainedetain from them any thing that is their due, when you lay more on them then they are able to bearebear, when any way you wrong or oppreſſeoppress them: thinkethink and ſaysay with your ſeluesselves, can this be iuſtifiedjustified? howHow ſhallshall we be able to hold vpup our head to our maſtermaster when he calleth vsus to account? What ſtrongerstronger motiuemotive to doedo all dutieduty? whatWhat ſtrongerstronger reſtraintrestraint from all iniuſticeinjustice and rigour? The conceit which many hauehave that they are free, vnderunder none, to giuegive no account, maketh them both negligent of their owneown dutieduty, and inſolentinsolent ouerover others; as Pharaoh, who ſaidsaid, Exod. 5. 2. Who is the Lord that I ſhouldshould obey him? and Sennacherib, who ſaidsaid, 2 Chr. 32. 15. Shall your God deliuerdeliver you out of mine hands? and Nebuchadnezzar, who ſaidsaid, Dan. 3. 15. Who is that God that ſhallshall deliuerdeliver you out of mine hands? NoteNotenote the iſſueissue of this inſolencyinsolency. Pharaoh after many extraordinarieextraordinary plagues laid on him and his people, Exod. 14. 28. was drowned in the red ſeasea with all his hoſthost. IſaIsa. 37. 36, 38. Sennacherib after his hoſthost was deſtroieddestroyed, was ſlaineslain by his owneown ſonnessons. Dan. 4. 30. Nebuchadnezzar became a very bruitbrute. But to let theſethese abominable blaſphemersblasphemers paſſepass, there be many maſtersmasters who, though they vtterutter not with their mouthesmouths ſuchsuch execrable blaſphemiesblasphemies, yet by their carriage towards their ſeruantsservants ſhewshow themſeluesthemselves to be little better minded, in that they make their owneown will a rule to their ſeruantsservants, and will hauehave them doedo ſuchsuch things as are vnmeetunmeet and vnlawfullunlawful, vſingusing their ſeruantsservants as ſlauesslaves, or rather as beaſtsbeasts. Let all ſuchsuch maſtersmasters know that they hauehave a maſtermaster.

div.head: §. 47. Of the equality betwixt maſtersmasters and ſeruantsservants in relation to God.
div.p: The ſecondsecond reaſonreason in this particle alſoalso (your maſtermaster alſoalso) declareth an equality betwixt maſtersmasters and ſeruantsservants in relation to God. As God is the maſtersmastermasters of ſeruantsservants, ſoso he is the maſtermaster of maſtersmasters alſoalso. As ſeruantsservants are the Lords 1 Cor. 7. 22. freemen, ſoso maſtersmasters are the Lords ſeruantsservants. In this reſpectrespect they who are made rulers, and they who are vnderunder them, are called Matt. 24. 49. d • ominus fidelem habens ſeruumseruum di'igat vt frat • rem propter fidei ſocietatemsocietatem ſaluasalua ſibisibi ſeruituteseruitute. ConſtitConstit. ApoſtApost. l. 4. c. 12. Dominum patrem familiae appellauerunt, ſeruosseruos familiares. Sen • ec. EpiſtEpist. 47. fellow ſeruantsservants. For howſoeuerhowsoever in outward dignity there is great difference betwixt maſtermaster and ſeruantservant, yet as the ſeruantsservants of God they are of a like condition, and in many things may be accounted equallequal: eſpeciallyespecially if both be of the ſamesame faith, and ſoso brethren in ChriſtChrist. This is another ſpurspur and curbecurb too.
A ſpurspur in that God will the more kindly accept that goodneſſegoodness which maſtersmasters doedo to their ſeruantsservants, becauſebecause it is done to Gods ſeruantsservants.
A curbecurb, in that ſeruantsservants ſhallshall be heard before God as well as maſtersmasters, for he is the maſtermaster of both.

Many thinkethink that all the kindneſſekindness which is ſhewedshowed to ſeruantsservants is loſtlost, becauſebecause they are ſoso meanemean as they are able to make no recompencerecompense. But their maſtermaster is able.

Others thinkethink, their ſeruantsservants can neuernever take any reuengerevenge of them, and thereupon vſeuse them as they liſtlist. But the maſtermaster of ſeruantsservants, who is alſoalso the maſtermaster of maſtersmasters, can take vengeance, eueneven ſuchsuch as ſhallshall make maſtersmasters ſorelysorely repent all the wrong they hauehave done.

If maſtersmasters did duelyduly weigh this point, that, howſoeuerhowsoever in regard of outward gouernmentgovernment there be ſomesome difference betwixt them and their ſeruantsservants, yet before God they are as fellow ſeruantsservants, would they be ouerover-rigorous and cruellcruel? wouldWould they not be kindekind and gentle?

div.head: §. 48. Of Gods being in heauenheaven, how it is a motiuemotive to prouokeprovoke maſtersmasters well to reſpectrespect their ſeruantsservants.
div.p: The third reaſonreason (taken from the place of God, in heauenheaven) declareth the ſurpaſſingsurpassing excellencieexcellency of that great maſtermaster, who is the common maſtermaster of maſtersmasters and of ſeruantsservants: and it addeth an edge to the former motiuesmotives.

1. It ſhewethshoweth that though the wrong which maſtersmasters doedo to their ſeruantsservants be within the walls of their houſehouse, ſoso as no mortallmortal eye can ſeesee it, yet God who is in heauenheaven ſeethseeth it: and though ſeruantsservants cannot be admitted into the courts of men to make their complaint, yet heauenheaven is open to them; to that great maſtermaster that is in heauenheaven they may hauehave acceſſeaccess when they will. That which made the euillevil ſtewardsteward dealedeal hardly with his fellowesfellows, was the conceit Mat. 24. 48. which he had of his maſtersmasters abſenceabsence. But no ſuchsuch conceit can they hauehave of this great maſtermaster, who know that he is in heauenheaven, and Pro. 15. 3. that as heauenheaven is ouerover eueryevery place, ſoso the eyes of the Lord are in eueryevery place, and behold the euillevil and good: he ſeethseeth all the good, and all the euillevil that maſtersmasters doedo to their ſeruantsservants.

2. It ſhewethshoweth that the kindneſſekindness which the Lord will repay, and the vengeance which he will inflict, is infinitely greater then the good or euillevil that maſtersmasters can doedo to their ſeruantsservants, eueneven as heauenheaven i,is higher then earth, and as he that is in heauenheaven is greater then they that are on earth. DoeſtDoest thou therefore, who art a maſtermaster on earth, reioycerejoice, or grieuegrieve the ſoulesoul of thy ſeruantservant? God in heauenheaven can much more make glad or ſadsad thy ſoulesoul. DoeſtDoest thou therefore deſiredesire the fauourfavour, or fearefear the frownesfrowns of thy maſtermaster in heauenheaven? ſhewShow fauourfavour to thy ſeruantservant on earth, and forbeareforbear threatningthreatening. Remember the infinite diſparitiedisparity betwixt thy maſterſhipmastership and Gods, and this will the more mouemove thee to dealedeal with thy ſeruantservant, as thou wouldeſtwouldest hauehave God dealedeal with thee.

3. It ſhewethshoweth that there is much more reaſonreason we ſhouldshould take notice of our ſeruantsservants, of their painespains, of their diligence, and of their faithfulneſſefaithfulness, then that God ſhouldshould take notice of ours: and leſſeless reaſonreason that we ſhouldshould ſcornescorn, or neglect our ſeruantsservants, then God ſcornescorn or neglect vsus. For there is far greater difference betwixt God and vsus, then betwixt vsus and our ſeruantsservants. We and our Vis tu cogitare iſtumistum quem ſeruumseruum tuum 〈◊〉 vocas, exijſdemexijsdem ſeminibusseminibus ortum, eodem fruicoelo, aequè ſpirarespirare, aequè viuere, aequè mori. Senec. EpiſtEpist. 47. ſeruantsservants are all of the earth, of the ſamesame mould, nature, and diſpoſitiondisposition, ſubiectsubject to the ſamesame paſſionpassion, and to the ſamesame diſſolutiondissolution. (The heathen obſeruedobserved as much.) But God is in heauenheaven, eternalleternal, vnchangeableunchangeable, eueryevery way ſurpaſſingsurpassing glorious. How can we then lookelook to be reſpectedrespected of this maſtermaster, if we reſpectrespect not our ſeruantsservants? O maſtersmasters, in all your dealings with your ſeruantsservants, remember your maſtermaster is in heauenheaven.

div.head: §. 49. Of Gods impartiallimpartial reſpectrespect of all.
div.p: The fourth reaſonreason (in theſethese words, neither is there reſpectrespect of perſonspersons with him) declareth Gods iuſtjust and equallequal manner of proceeding with all men, of what rankerank and degree ſoeuersoever. God will doedo the ſamesame things to all ſortssorts of maſtersmasters that they doedo to their ſeruantsservants. To the conſiderationconsideration of this impartiallimpartial iuſticejustice of God doth the ApoſtleApostle call maſtersmasters, both becauſebecause of that outward power which they hauehave ouerover their ſeruantsservants, and alſoalso becauſebecause for the moſtmost part maſtersmasters are backtbacked with the power and authority of magiſtratesmagistrates on earth, who in matters of difference betwixt maſtermaster and ſeruantservant are ordinarily partiallpartial, reſpectingrespecting maſtersmasters more then ſeruantsservants.

But let maſtersmasters here learnelearn to caſtcast off all ſuchsuch fond conceits, and fooliſhfoolish hopes. Though they be higher in place, hauehave more wealth, and better friends then their ſeruantsservants, and though men who hauehave carnallcarnal eieseyes may thereby be much mouedmoved to reſpectrespect them, yet will not God goego an haireshairs bredthbreadth from iuſticejustice for the whole world. If the greateſtgreatest man that euerever was in the world ſhouldshould hauehave a ſeruantservant that were the meaneſtmeanest that euerever was, and a caſecase betwixt that maſtermaster and that ſeruantservant ſhouldshould come before God, God would not any whit at all leanelean to that maſtermaster more then to the ſeruantservant.
